value.body: Disaster management associates work on preparing communities for floods, cyclones, droughts and other hazards, and on coordinating relief when they strike. Employers include NGOs, humanitarian agencies, development consultancies and CSR programmes. Day-to-day work mixes field visits, community training, data collection and report writing, with long hours during emergencies.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA in Geography, Sociology or Social Work; a disaster management diploma helps

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, survey apps, basic GIS, report templates

items.label: Policy framework
items.note: Sets up national, state and district disaster management authorities

items.label: NDRF battalions
items.note: Drawn from central armed police forces; sanctioned strength ~18,500

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually enter as project or field associates on NGO and agency programmes, often on fixed-term project contracts. A postgraduate diploma or certificate in disaster management, field volunteering and a local language for the project area make an application stronger.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many roles are tied to project funding and run on contracts of one to three years.
Field postings can be in remote or disaster-affected areas.
Common next steps: project officer, programme coordinator, or a master's in disaster management.
